sections.h2: Where is St. Mary's County, Maryland, and what is its geography?
sections.html:
St. Mary's County sits on a peninsula at the southern tip of Southern Maryland, with the Patuxent River to the northeast, the Chesapeake Bay to the east, the Potomac River to the southwest and the Wicomico River to the west. The county's economic overview puts it about 38 miles southeast of Washington, D.C. and 90 miles south of Baltimore, with more than 500 miles of shoreline.

Total area is 764 square miles, but only 357 of those are land. Water makes up 53% of the county, which makes it the second largest Maryland county by total area. The interior is hilly with forest and farmland, and the coast has clay and sand bluffs along with low beaches and tidal marshes.

sections.h2: What communities make up St. Mary's County?
sections.html:
The county's largest community is California, and its seat is Leonardtown. Other named places include Lexington Park, Great Mills, Piney Point, Mechanicsville, Charlotte Hall, Loveville, Saint Inigoes, Scotland, Morganza, Point Lookout and St. Mary's City.

The state's 2025 county brief lists the largest places in the 2020 census as Lexington Park at 13,317, California at 12,947 and Leonardtown at 4,745.

sections.h2: What is the history of St. Mary's County?
sections.html:
St. Mary's City was the first capital of Maryland, and the capital stayed there for more than 50 years until it moved to Annapolis in 1695. Settlers landed on St. Clement's Island on March 25, 1634, and the county was established in 1637.

Tourism still builds on that history. Historic St. Mary's City, Point Lookout State Park and Sotterley Plantation are the best known sites.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers in St. Mary's County?
sections.html:
Naval Air Station Patuxent River is by far the largest. It hosts Naval Air Systems Command and the Naval Test Pilot School, and the state's 2025 county brief lists these top employers:

sections.h2: How do people travel in and out of St. Mary's County?
sections.html:
Maryland Route 235 and Route 5 are the main state highways, with Routes 4, 6, 234 and 245 also serving the county. St. Mary's Transit runs local service, and the Maryland Transit Administration operates commuter bus service to Washington.

The nearest commercial airports are Reagan National and Baltimore Washington International. Captain Walter Duke Regional Airport handles general aviation. The state brief reports that 11,817 residents, about 20%, commute out of the county for work.

sections.h2: What does the climate and coastline mean for a St. Mary's County house?
sections.html:
The county has a humid subtropical climate, with Leonardtown averaging 36.3 degrees in January and 78.1 degrees in July. The more useful local fact for an owner is the shoreline: coastal bluffs protect many areas from storm surge, while low-lying coastal land and tidal marshes are more exposed.

If your house is near the water, check flood exposure and the condition of any bulkhead or shoreline structure before you set a price. A house on a private well or septic system has its own sale steps.

  • Under Maryland Real Property Section 10-713, a contract for a house with a private well must require water quality testing as a condition of sale. Results stay valid for three years, and the buyer can waive the test in writing.
  • Anyone performing a septic inspection for a property transfer has needed a license from the Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals since July 1, 2022. The state says to contact its On-Site Systems Division at 410-537-3778 for county requirements.

sections.h2: How is property tax assessed and billed in St. Mary's County?
sections.html:
The State Department of Assessments and Taxation values the property, and the St. Mary's County Treasurer sends and collects the bill at 23150 Leonard Hall Drive, Leonardtown. The Treasurer's office number is 301-475-4200, extension 3300.

The fiscal 2026 county real property rate is 0.8478. The county's tax bill estimator shows separate lines for county, state, fire tax, rescue and support, along with flat fees and a county homestead credit line.

  • Maryland reassesses each property every three years and spreads the increase equally over three years.
  • For state tax purposes, a home's annual assessment increase above 10% is not taxed. Counties can set a lower cap.
  • You can appeal a new assessment within 45 days of the notice date. The next steps are the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board within 30 days of the final notice and then the Maryland Tax Court within 30 days of the board's order.
  • The county gets its tax file from the State on July 1, so ownership data updates once a year. Searching by address or parcel number is more reliable than searching by name.

sections.h2: What happens at the St. Mary's County annual tax sale?
sections.html:
The county holds its tax sale every year on the first Friday of March, covering the prior tax year. Owners of delinquent accounts are advertised in a local newspaper for four weeks before the sale. The most recent sale on the county page was held online on March 6, 2026, at 10:00 a.m.

The winning bidder receives a Certificate of Sale, which allows legal proceedings but does not give title or possession. If the owner redeems, the bidder gets back the taxes paid plus 6% annual interest through the month of redemption. If the owner does not redeem, the bidder may start court steps to foreclose the right to redeem. Properties are sold as is, and liens may survive the sale.

An owner who falls behind should treat the sale date as a hard deadline. Unpaid water and sewer bills, service charges and penalties are also first liens against the property, and MetCom handles those bills.

sections.h2: What costs and taxes come up when selling a St. Mary's County house?
sections.html:
Ask your settlement company about the county transfer and recordation taxes. The state's 2026 guide says St. Mary's County's transfer tax is limited by state law to 1%, with the first $30,000 of the buyer's principal residence price exempt, and that part of the recordation tax revenue goes to rural land conservation. It does not give the rate in force, so get that figure from the company handling your closing.

Also expect a payoff of any property tax due at settlement. The county posts bills and a payment portal online, and you can change a mailing address through the Treasurer's address change form. If back taxes are close to the tax sale, a cash offer with a quick closing can be a way to clear them, but compare it against a listing and ask for terms in writing.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of St. Mary's County?
faqs.a: Leonardtown is the county seat. California is the largest community, and Lexington Park is the other major population center near Naval Air Station Patuxent River.

faqs.q: What is the St. Mary's County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The fiscal 2026 county real property rate is 0.8478, according to the state's rate table. Your bill also shows state, fire, rescue and support lines, so the total depends on where the house sits.

faqs.q: When is the St. Mary's County tax sale?
faqs.a: The county holds its annual tax sale on the first Friday of March for the prior tax year. The 2026 sale was held online on March 6 at 10:00 a.m.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a St. Mary's County property assessment?
faqs.a: File within 45 days of the notice date with the local assessment office. Later levels are the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board and the Maryland Tax Court, each with a 30 day window.

faqs.q: Do I need to test the well before selling a St. Mary's County house?
faqs.a: If the house has a private well, Maryland Real Property Section 10-713 requires the contract to call for water testing as a condition of sale unless the buyer waives it in writing. Test results are valid for three years.
